the dative form δόρει [with the spear]

Hermann restored δόρει [with the spear] for δορί [with the spear] as the meter demands: Sophocles seems to have used this dative form consistently, since in all his examples the meter either demands or allows δόρει [with the spear]; I have discussed this in my Lexicon Sophocleum p. 125. Aeschylus, as the examples cited above show, and Euripides used both forms. Therefore it is uncertain whether in Aeschylus at the end of trimeters δορί [with the spear] or δόρει [with the spear] should be written, on which see what I said in the Thesaurus vol. 2 p. 1644.
